name: Verdance

stars.name: Verdance
stars.notes: Mature G-class star, exceptionally stable output with negligible flare activity, older and calmer than Sol

planets.name: Ashfall
planets.notes: Tidally stressed inner world with constant volcanic resurfacing, lava rivers visible from orbit

planets.name: Tanglewood
planets.notes: Lush temperate world dominated by continent-spanning forests, population 1.8 billion, system capital

planets.name: Caldera
planets.notes: 95% ocean coverage with volcanic island chains, population 340 million in floating cities and island settlements

planets.name: Dustwalk
planets.notes: Arid but habitable along polar ice caps, population 28 million, agricultural domes and terraforming efforts underway

planets.name: Titan's Cradle
planets.notes: Banded orange-and-cream gas giant, three of its moons harbor small research stations

planets.name: Farwatch
planets.notes: Distant ice world used as a long-range sensor platform, automated deep-space observation post

asteroid_belts.name: Greenstone Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Named for unusually high olivine content giving fragments a green hue, active mining operations supply construction materials

stations.name: Verdance Prime Orbital
stations.notes: System's main port of entry, shipyards, commercial hub, and administrative center

stations.name: Tide Market
stations.notes: Specialized trading station for oceanic harvests and aquaculture exports

stations.name: Hearthstone Station
stations.notes: Ring habitat for deep-system workers and families, self-sustaining agricultural bays

faction_control.notes: Stable democratic government with strong environmental protection laws, member of the Elysian Compact trade alliance

history: First colonized in 2318 by the Elysian Expedition, a coalition of agrarian communities seeking worlds suitable for large-scale sustainable settlement.
Tanglewood's biosphere proved remarkably compatible with Terran crops, and by 2400 the system had become the breadbasket of the sector, exporting food to dozens of neighboring systems.

The passage of the Forest Covenant in 2589 permanently protected 60% of Tanglewood's native forests, establishing the Verdance Commonality's reputation as an ecological steward among spacefaring civilizations.
description: Verdance is the jewel of the Elysian Marches—a mature yellow star presiding over a system that seems almost impossibly hospitable. Three of its six worlds support permanent populations, and the warm, steady light of its aging G-class primary has nurtured complex biospheres on two of them. From Tanglewood's towering forests to Caldera's endless sapphire oceans, Verdance offers vistas that remind humanity why it left Earth: not to escape, but to find what else the galaxy might offer.

With nearly 2.2 billion inhabitants spread across three worlds and several orbital stations, Verdance is one of the most populous systems in the sector. Its agricultural output is staggering—Tanglewood alone feeds fifteen neighboring systems—and the Greenstone Belt provides a steady stream of construction materials. Heavy trade traffic flows through Verdance Prime Orbital daily, carrying grain, timber, fish, refined minerals, and manufactured goods to destinations across the Elysian Compact.

Yet Verdance's prosperity attracts envy and carries its own tensions. The Forest Covenant is beloved by Tanglewood's residents but resented by developers who see billions of credits locked away in protected timber. Caldera's floating cities are increasingly autonomous, and whispers of a separatist movement trouble the Commonality's legislators. Meanwhile, Farwatch's deep-space sensors have detected anomalous signals from beyond the system's edge—faint, structured, and distinctly non-natural. The Commonality has quietly increased Farwatch's funding, but has yet to make any public announcement about what its telescopes may have found.
